name: synthesized-terminal-envelope
description: warren-9a4a: the in-pod agent entrypoint synthesizes a terminal agent_end envelope when the agent exits without one (isTerminalEnvelope tracks parsed events via src/core/event-envelope.ts extractAgentEventEnvelope; emitSynthesizedTerminalEnvelope emits post-exit with stopReason error on non-zero exit). Reap terminalizes ONLY on result|agent_end on the state_change/system carrier, so any new in-pod kill path must leave a terminal envelope behind or the run hangs in running.

name: k8s-salvage-window
description: K8s in-pod salvage (src/runtime/k8s/salvage.ts) commits a dirty tree with the bot identity BEFORE push/bundle captures, and the agent container carries WARREN_GIT_TOKEN harness-only: defaultSpawn scrubs it via agentChildEnv (agent-io.ts), finalize-entrypoint falls back to it in no_intent windows. FinalizeGitRunner opts.env supports undefined=delete for the GIT_* repo-context scrub.

name: salvage-trigger-decision
description: warren-985e: pod-side salvage triggers are decided by salvageTriggerForResult() in src/runtime/k8s/salvage-post.ts over the collected FinalizeResult (push_failed | empty_push_dirty); a SUCCESSFUL zero-commit push with a dirty tree is a loss window too — the pushed branch carries nothing. New wire enums go in src/core/wire.ts, which sits exactly at its frozen check:size budget, so adding vocabulary requires condensing comments elsewhere in the file.

name: pod-driven-finalize-recovery
description: warren-5202: control-plane-restart recovery for in-pod finalize is POD-DRIVEN, not sweep-driven — the pod's own GET /runs/:id/finalize-intent poll is the only signal that survives every restart shape (log rotation can erase the terminal envelope, and the agent+finalize share one container so pod status can't distinguish 'agent running' from 'awaiting intent'). Pattern: handler reports intent misses to a boot-wired FinalizeRecoveryHook (src/runs/finalize-recovery.ts); grace + single-flight + coordinator re-check prevent racing the healthy reap path; outcome classified from a new ?agent_exit= poll hint, then the persisted event log, then a succeeded default. Terminal/gone pods stay with the warren-c433 watchdog reconcile net.

name: entrypoint-agent-uid-split
description: warren-cb93: the k8s agent container runs warren's entrypoint at uid 1000 and setpriv-drops the AGENT process to uid 1001 (gid stays the fsGroup 1000) so a forged write at /proc/1/fd/1 fails EACCES. Key mechanics: the container adds caps [SETUID, SETGID, KILL] for the ENTRYPOINT only (KILL because the stdin-hold watchdog now signals cross-uid); the drop relies on the runtime propagating AMBIENT caps to a non-root pid 1 (containerd/runc do — under no_new_privs, ambient is the ONLY channel that survives execve, file caps are dead); the entrypoint preflights with 'setpriv ... -- true' and fails closed; workspace stays writable via fsGroup + umask 002 in BOTH workspace-init.ts and agent-entrypoint.ts; git safe.directory '*' is uid-agnostic (warren-fd08) so a uid-1001 agent commits in a uid-1000-owned checkout. DockerProvider is unaffected — it spawns the agent argv directly as pid 1, no entrypoint fd exists. Escape hatch: WARREN_K8S_AGENT_UID_DROP=0.

Live GKE dogfood run run_m0hb8t6a7et8 failed before model startup because the non-root agent entrypoint did not receive SETUID/SETGID; setpriv uid-drop preflight exited 127 and Warren misleadingly finalized no_model_response.
resolution: With explicit operator authorization, set WARREN_K8S_AGENT_UID_DROP=0 on deployment/warren and verified rollout before redispatch; track restoration of split-UID isolation and better failure classification in warren-950d.

title: uid-drop-live-restoration-warren-950d
rationale: The seed required removing the escape hatch only after a successful split-UID canary; both the deploy-gate canary pod and a real dispatched run proved the split before the hatch came off.

description: deploy-gke's per-resource apply loop means a red deploy job does not imply the rollout failed: only the resources that errored are stale. Run 33537106880 failed on the warren-run-pods Role (SA lacks container.roles.update) while the Deployment applied and rolled out the new image fine.
resolution: Check kubectl -n warren get deploy/warren image before assuming a failed deploy left the old build live; apply the failed resource manually from a workstation, and grant the WIF SA container.roles.update for the durable fix (warren-2a26).

title: K8s workspace-init uses a blobless partial clone without the repo cache
rationale: Removes the need for the 1 TiB Filestore cache (warren-8175) without breaking base-commit pinning (warren-919a); --depth was rejected because it breaks merge-base and pinning.

description: Dispatching many 16 GiB run pods in parallel stalls on the regional SSD_TOTAL_GB quota (us-west1 500 GB): each pod forces its own e2-highmem-4 node with a ~100 GB boot disk, so the 5th node fails with 'GCE quota exceeded' and pods sit Pending for 25+ min. August data showed p95 run-pod memory at 1.6 GiB, all >2 GiB pods were openclaw.
resolution: Set WARREN_K8S_MEMORY_REQUEST_MIB=LIMIT=4096 (operator-approved 2026-09-03, repo variables recorded); several run pods now pack per node.

description: Autopilot rejects pods whose nodeSelector uses topology.gke.io/zone (Warden: key not allowed); a static PV's nodeAffinity with that key is fine and is enough to pin the pod to the disk's zone.
resolution: Drop the pod nodeSelector; rely on the PV nodeAffinity (verified restoring a PD snapshot into a throwaway postgres pod).

description: Plan-runs on GKE failed child_provider_error with 'agent exited 137 without emitting a terminal envelope' (2026-09-03, 2026-09-15). Root cause was GCE Spot preemption of the node under the run pods, four times in 35 minutes; the in-pod entrypoint's own proc.kill on SIGTERM yields exit 137, which it then labels oom_killed, and reap labels provider_error.
resolution: Read the run's system events first: cancel_requested{SIGTERM} then oom_killed{137} means the pod got a kubelet SIGTERM, not an OOM or provider fault. Two pods dying in the same second share a node. Confirm in Cloud Logging with protoPayload.methodName=compute.instances.preempted on the gk3-warren-nap node about 40s after the kill. Warren's own pods.delete audit entry lands about 5s AFTER the kill (reap cleanup) and is not the cause. Mitigation is WARREN_K8S_SPOT=0; the misclassification is warren-a757 and retry exhaustion is warren-c6bc.

description: Judge 'kill' on 2026-09-15 only blanked JUDGE_CALIBRATION_MODEL in the gke-live-judge overlay — that pauses the calibration re-judge, not the primary judge loop. The Deployment stayed at replicas=1, so the 09-16 GKE deploy's 'kubectl set image deploy/judge' rolled a fresh pod and it looked resurrected.
resolution: Kill an opt-in extension by replicas=0 (kubectl scale + pin 'replicas: 0' in the gitignored overlay) or by deleting the Deployment. deploy-gke.yml only runs set image, which never changes replicas and skips when the Deployment is absent, so either stays dead across deploys. Verify with kubectl get deploy, not by env.

name: gvisor-cold-node-admission
description: On GKE Autopilot the first gVisor run pod after idle waits ~2 min in Admitted while a sandbox node provisions (k8s.pod_warning 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'). For demos, dispatch a throwaway gVisor run a few minutes ahead to warm the node.

title: Run-scoped token authorizes K8s git-credential remint
rationale: The pod cannot hold an expiring App installation token, so the remint must ride the run-scoped callback channel; the route+own-id+liveness gate keeps it pinned to the caller's own live run, and the handler mints a fresh forge credential rather than echoing the caller's token (warren-5a5c).

name: live-run-monitoring-via-state-poll-plus-stream-tail
description: Monitoring a live K8s run: GET /runs/:id/events tails the live stream and never closes (a full download only completes at terminal), so poll run state via GET /runs/:id every ~55s and, to check progress, background-download the event stream to a file and inspect its tail — event ts freshness proves the agent is alive.

name: k8s-spot-preemption-classification
description: warren-ea4b: Spot preemption classified as a new retryable RunFailureReason 'preempted' (src/core/wire.ts + TerminalReason in runtime/contract.ts), witnesses in k8s/status-map.ts (reason Terminated/Shutdown + node-shutdown message, DisruptionTarget/TerminationByKubelet) and the vanished-pod arm via PodWatcher.deletedSpotNode + K8sProvider.preemptedPods; a 30s spot-node label poll in runtime-wiring.ts detects deleted gke-spot nodes. Ratchet note: provider.ts/wire.ts/contract.ts sit at frozen size ceilings — trimming pre-existing comment lines was required to add net code.

gVisor (GKE Sandbox) breaks warren's uid-1000 file-caps setpriv split: admission rejects allowPrivilegeEscalation=true, no_new_privs makes file caps inert, and gVisor drops ambient caps across a root->1000 setpriv (runc keeps them). setpriv also rejects --securebits +keep_caps. Working posture: entrypoint uid 0 inside the sandbox with caps SETUID/SETGID/KILL and allowPrivilegeEscalation=false, agent still dropped to 1001 (pod-runtime-class.ts).
resolution: Use resources.runtimeClass, which applies sandboxedAgentSecurityContext; never re-enable allowPrivilegeEscalation for sandboxed pods.

name: gvisor-spike-2026-09-25
description: Spike 2026-09-25 on GKE Autopilot: gVisor bun install --frozen-lockfile is 2.8x slower than runc (29.5s vs 10.7s); clone 1.2x, bun test 1.2x. Metadata server 169.254.169.254 was reachable from run pods on BOTH runtimes; only the NetworkPolicy except blocks it. us-west1 SSD_TOTAL_GB quota raised to 750 (each Autopilot node takes a 100GB boot disk).

gVisor ignores PR_CAPBSET_DROP: after setpriv --bounding-set=-all the agent's CapBnd still reads 0xe0 under runsc. Harmless because no_new_privs=1 and uid 1001 (setresuid(0) EPERM, /proc/1/environ and kill -0 1 denied), verified live 2026-09-25. Also: the agent image has no bc; use awk for arithmetic in run prompts.
resolution: Do not rely on the bounding set under gVisor; no_new_privs + non-root uid is the boundary.

name: gvisor-bench-n3-2026-09-25
description: N=3 per arm through real warren runs (claude-code, same prompt): clone 2.6s runc vs 4.3s gVisor; bun install --frozen-lockfile 3.4s vs 62.6s (~18x, gVisor very stable +-0.3s); bun test src/core 0.20s vs 0.46s. Run pods only; film instance warren-film.

GKE Dataplane V2: NetworkPolicy ipBlock except 169.254.0.0/16 does not block pod-to-own-node traffic; run pods reach kubelet at the gateway 169.254.4.6:10250 (401, anonymous auth off). setpriv --bounding-set=-all does not take effect on runc or gVisor (CapBnd 0xe0); no_new_privs is the real boundary.
resolution: Tracked as warren-3584; kubelet authn + no SA token are the current controls.

description: Treating exit 137 as OOM misclassified spot preemption; a dying node SIGKILLs the agent too (warren-a757)
resolution: Only terminated.reason==OOMKilled means OOM; read DisruptionTarget/NodeNotReady pod signals for node loss
